documents.prompt: Graph the solution set of $y\ge {{m}}x{{b|signed}}$ by constructing its boundary and shading the correct half-plane.

solutionReview.headline: Graph the boundary $y={{m}}x{{b|signed}}$ as a solid line, then shade above it.
reasoning: Boundary: graph $y={{m}}x{{b|signed}}$. Start at the y-intercept $(0,{{b}})$ and use the slope ${{m}}$: one step right reaches $(1,{{p}})$. Draw the line through these two points.
Line style: $\ge$ includes equality, so the points on the boundary are solutions and the line is solid.
Shading: $y\ge {{m}}x{{b|signed}}$ keeps the points whose y-value is at or above the line, so shade above. Check $(0,{{t}})$: ${{t}}\ge {{b}}$ is true, and that point lies above the line.
solutionReview.commonError: Choosing the side from the slope instead of the symbol. Solved for $y$, $\ge$ always means above the boundary, whether the slope ${{m}}$ is positive or negative.
solutionReview.answerSummary: Solid line through $(0,{{b}})$ and $(1,{{p}})$, which is $y={{m}}x{{b|signed}}$, with the half-plane above it shaded.

attemptFeedback: Check the boundary points first, then line style, then which side is shaded.
supportHints: For $y>mx+b$ or $y\ge mx+b$, shade above; for $y<mx+b$ or $y\le mx+b$, shade below.

documents.prompt: A feasible plan is represented by $y\le {{m}}x{{b|signed}}$. Construct the TWO-VARIABLE solution graph that shows every feasible ordered pair.

solutionReview.headline: Every point in a half-plane can be a solution.
reasoning: Use the equation $y={{m}}x{{b|signed}}$ for the boundary.
Because the inequality is inclusive and uses $\le$, draw a solid boundary and shade below it.

attemptFeedback: A two-variable inequality solution is a region, not one number or one interval on a number line.
supportHints: Pick two x-values to construct the boundary line, then apply the inequality symbol.
